item.title: The ABC-equation revisited: missed (quasi) integrable cases. Part II: extensions and actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue here the study of the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$ and using the results obtained in the first part construct new quasi-integrable structures and compute their actions on symmetries and cosymmetries.
item.dc:creator: I. S. Krasil'shchik

item.title: Painlev\'e II connection problem revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.28227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the inhomogeneous Painlev\'e II equation for generic monodromy data. Using Kapaev's asymptotic formulas, the parameters of Zak transform representations of the Painlev\'e II tau function on six special rays $\arg t=\frac{\pi p}{3}$ ($p=0,\ldots,5$) in the complex time plane are expressed in terms of Stokes parameters of the associated linear system. We then solve the connection problem for the tau function between these special rays, and provide analytical and numerical checks of our result.
item.dc:creator: Nikolai Iorgov, Oleg Lisovyy, Noam Tamarin, Yurii Zhuravlov

item.title: A twisted Marchenko lemma and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.28233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a twisted Marchenko lemma with applications into non-commutative two-component integrable systems. Starting from a twisted differential equation, we introduce the corresponding two-component Wronski matrix $W_{n,m}(\boldsymbol\phi,\boldsymbol\psi)$. Under the Marchenko lemma conditions, the logarithmic derivative $(\partial W_{n,m})W_{n,m}^{-1}$ satisfies nonlinear equations, whose two-component projections yield a non-commutative two-component KP equation, while a single-component reduction recovers the non-commutative Burgers equation, KP equation and DS equation. A direct approach based on two-component quasi-Wronskians is developed, from which a higher-order non-commutative two-component KP equation is generated with matrix-valued solutions. Reductions of the seed functions of the non-commutative two-component KP hierarchy yield the one-component counterpart, while a stepwise reduction of those for the two-component KP equation gives the non-commutative DS and NLS equations.
item.dc:creator: Jun-Yang Zhang, Shi-Hao Li, Shou-Feng Shen

item.title: Toda chain solves large BKP
item.description: arXiv:2610.28492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that any solution of the Toda chain hierarchy (the 1D reduction of the 2D Toda lattice) is a solution of the large BKP hierarchy. This is a difference analogue of Alexandrov's result that KdV solves (small) BKP.
item.dc:creator: Anton Zabrodin

item.title: Boundary One-Point Functions in the Open XXZ Spin Chain with Generic Integrable Boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.27062v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.
item.dc:creator: Till Bargheer, Tengis Batmunkh, Paul Ryan

item.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27420v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the Yamazaki-Hori solution to the Ernst equation can be represented in the Pfaffian form. We also discuss the consequences of this result for Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the Ernst equation and the 2D Toda model.
item.dc:creator: Arsen Melikyan, Aleksandr Pinzul

item.title: Surface defects on lens space and transfer matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.28165v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study surface defects in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories of class $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories of class $\mathcal{S}_k$ placed on $L(r,1)\times S^1$. The lens space index depends on the fugacities $p$ and $q$, and the effect of the defects on it is captured by difference operators acting on the fugacities and holonomies of flavor symmetries. For theories of type $A_1$ we determine in closed form the difference operators for the basic defects, labeled by $p^r$, $q^r$ and $pq$, and show that for odd $r$ there exist additional elementary defects, whose operators shift the holonomy by one half modulo $r$. All the operators commute, and the elementary operators generate the others. For even $r$ the same holds once the holonomy is extended to a twisted sector. We show that the elementary operators are traces of $L$-operators whose entries generate a Sklyanin algebra, with nome $q^r$ and shift $pq$. The lens space enters only through the parameters of the algebra and through its representation, which is realized on a doubled holonomy label. The $p$- and $q$-type algebras form a lens space version of the elliptic modular double. For class $\mathcal{S}_k$ theories we propose, and test in several ways, that the defect operators are transfer matrices of inhomogeneous spin chains built from these $L$-operators. Throughout, we use the TQFT structure of the lens space index, which follows from S-duality, both to fix and to check the operators.
item.dc:creator: Kazunobu Maruyoshi, Toshihiro Ota, Masahito Yamazaki

item.title: The gauge action on semi-discrete Lax representations, its invariants, and Lax-Miura type constructions
item.description: arXiv:2604.20830v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce and study explicit invariants with respect to the action of (local) gauge transformations on the set of semi-discrete (differential-difference) matrix Lax representations (MLRs) for a given (1+1)-dimensional evolutionary differential-difference equation with any number of components. Using these invariants, we obtain the following general results: - Sufficient conditions for nonremovability of parameters in semi-discrete MLRs. (Nonremovability by means of gauge transformations.) - Necessary conditions for two semi-discrete MLRs to be gauge equivalent. Effective use of these results is demonstrated. We present the general theory and apply it to MLRs for equations of Volterra--Yamilov, Cherdantsev--Yamilov, Toda types and Miura-type modifications. Also, we present a comparison with results of S. Yu. Sakovich and M. Marvan on gauge invariants for (continuous) zero-curvature representations of partial differential equations. Furthermore, we demonstrate procedures for constructing Miura-type transformations (MTs) for discrete (partial difference) equations (on the two-dimensional integer lattice) by means of gauge simplifications of discrete matrix Lax pairs (DLPs) and reductions of auxiliary systems associated with DLPs. This allows us to construct new MTs for (non-evolutionary) 4-point and 6-point discrete equations from [D. Levi, R.I. Yamilov, J. Phys. A 2009], [S. Konstantinou-Rizos, A.V. Mikhailov, P. Xenitidis, J. Math. Phys. 2015].
item.dc:creator: Sergei Igonin

item.title: Generalized mKdV Equation and Genus Two Jacobi Type Hyperelliptic Differential Equation
item.description: arXiv:2511.02621v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generalized the mKdV equation in order that the static equations include ${\rm sn}$ differential equation. As a result, a good correspondence was obtained between the KdV equation and the mKdV equation.For general genus two hyperelliptic curves, we obtained differential equations for Weierstrass type and Jacobi type hyperelliptic functions. Considering the special case of $\lambda_6=0, \lambda_0=0$, Weierstrass type and Jacobi type hyperelliptic functions are different solutions to the same hyperelliptic differential equations. Then these solutions are connected by the special ${\rm Sp(4, {\bf R})}$ Lie group transformation.
item.dc:creator: Masahito Hayashi, Kazuyasu Shigemoto, Takuya Tsukioka
